title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 220 (Seizure of documents by inspector)

content.overview: Section 220 provides that where in the course of an investigation an inspector has reasonable ground to believe that the books and papers of, or relating to, any company or other body corporate or managing director or manager of such company are likely to be destroyed, mutilated, altered, falsified or secreted, he may, after obtaining an order from the Special Court or Magistrate for that purpose, enter and search the place where such books or papers are kept and seize them. Seized books are retained only for the period the section allows and then returned, subject to taking copies or extracts. The power is preservative and does not transfer title.
content.glance: Inspector with reasonable ground that books may be destroyed/falsified → order from Special Court/Magistrate → enter, search and seize; return within statutory period; preservation power, not transfer of title.
content.study: Where in the course of investigation under this Chapter or under section 210, 212, 213 or 216 the inspector has reasonable ground to believe that the books and papers of, or relating to, any company or other body corporate or managing director or manager of such company or other body corporate may be destroyed, mutilated, altered, falsified or secreted, the inspector may after obtaining an order from the Special Court for the seizure of such books and papers, enter and search the place or places where such books or papers are kept and seize such books and papers. Current-law framing: confirm ongoing investigation under the Chapter or specified sections; establish reasonable ground regarding destruction or falsification; obtain Special Court/Magistrate order; enter, search and seize; retain only for the permitted period and return. Distinct from Registrar seizure under s. 209, which applies at the inspection stage.

sections.heading: Trigger
sections.body: During investigation under the Chapter or ss. 210/212/213/216: reasonable ground that books of the company, related body corporate, MD or manager may be destroyed, mutilated, altered, falsified or secreted.

sections.heading: Order
sections.body: Prior order from the Special Court (or Magistrate as provided) for seizure.

sections.heading: Search and Seize
sections.body: Enter and search the place where books are kept and seize them.

sections.heading: Return
sections.body: Retain only for the period the section states; return subject to copies or extracts; no transfer of title.

examples.title: Seizure during investigation
examples.body: During a s. 210 investigation the inspector has reasonable ground that statutory registers are about to be destroyed. After obtaining a Special Court order, he may enter, search and seize under s. 220.

examples.title: Distinct from s. 209
examples.body: Section 209 is the Registrar/inspector seizure power at the inspection stage. Section 220 is the parallel power for an inspector during a formal investigation under the Chapter.

hypotheticals.question: May an inspector seize books under s. 220 without any court order?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Section 220 requires an order from the Special Court (or Magistrate as the section provides) before entry, search and seizure.

distinctions.title: Seizure by inspector during investigation (s. 220) vs search and seizure at inspection (s. 209)
distinctions.left: Inspector during investigation under Chapter XIV / ss. 210–216
distinctions.right: Registrar or inspector at inspection/inquiry stage under s. 206

misconceptions.trap: Seizure under s. 220 permanently transfers the books to the Government.
misconceptions.correction: Seizure is preservative. Books are retained only for the period the section allows and then returned; title does not pass.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 220 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: I. Confirm ongoing investigation. II. Test reasonable ground. III. Confirm court order. IV. Apply seize and return. V. Conclude.

questionsAndAnswers.question: What should submissions contain?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Investigation status; belief facts; order; seizure scope; precise relief.

learningObjectives: State the conditions for seizure by an inspector under s. 220.
Distinguish s. 220 from s. 209 inspection-stage seizure.
enhancement.definition: Section 220 allows an inspector, during investigation, on reasonable ground that books may be destroyed or falsified, to obtain a court order and seize those books, returning them within the statutory period.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Evidence preservation during formal investigation is authorised by court order without converting seizure into a transfer of title.
essentialIngredients: Ongoing investigation under the Chapter or specified sections
Reasonable ground that books may be destroyed or falsified
Order from Special Court or Magistrate
Seize and return within permitted period
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 220 is the investigation-stage seizure power parallel to s. 209 at inspection.
enhancement.problemApplication: Confirm investigation; test belief; require order; apply return.
